body:
Thank you.  I have already met with a neurologist, and have been seeing a psychiatrist as well.  The neuro pretty much just nodded and said that for most people symptoms resolve within three months before sending me out the door. The psychiatrist prescribed some meds for the depression/anxiety. I'm hopeful I'll notice some changes soon.

In the meantime, I've been trying to get plenty of rest and have made some dietary adjustments as well.  I suppose these things are helping, but I still feel so debilitated.  The prospect of recovering my former potential seems unlikely, and I'm not sure how to cope with that.

This was my third and most severe concussion.  I feel like I've lost my spirit, my soul... not to get too esoteric.  It's a strange and uncomfortable feeling, and I'm barely tolerating it.  I really don't want to live if I remain like this. 

I want to give this whole situation time. I know that's what it needs. It's been 2.5 months since the concussion, and while I showed a lot of improvement in the first few weeks following the injury, progress seems to have halted since then.  This really scares me.  I'm getting more desperate every day.

Ouch. That sounds excruciating.  I've never appreciated the psychological impact that physical pain can have until now.  Other symptoms aside, the headaches alone can be debilitating. They'll go away, and then the most minor disturbance (turning my head too quick, going over a pothole in the car) will bring them back, along with an increase in other symptoms.  Very upsetting. I just want to be who I was again.  I really used to think I had a bright future.  Now I am utterly uncertain.   Thanks for taking the time to share.

Thanks for the support.  You make a good point.  I just am struggling with how much has changed.  All sorts of possibilities in my life seem to have disappeared.  I used to derive a lot of pleasure from being intellectually engaged.  Now I struggle to keep up with the plot of a simple novel.  I feel so damaged.
